about.game.f1: Play the computer: 12 levels from beginner to expert, with move hints and a practice Elo.
about.game.f2: Two players, one device: play on the same phone, with Black's pieces facing the player sitting opposite.
about.game.f3: Play online: find a random opponent or invite friends with a link, with clocks and Glicko-2 ratings.
about.game.f4: Puzzles: mate-in-1 and mate-in-2 problems, with a Puzzle Rating that measures your tactical skill.
about.game.f6: 2D and 3D boards, many piece sets and board colours, light/dark themes, 20 languages.

rules.castle.text: The King moves 2 squares towards a Rook, then that Rook jumps over to the square right next to the King on the other side. You may castle only if neither the King nor that Rook has moved, there are no pieces between them, the King is not in check, and it does not pass through or land on an attacked square.
rules.castle.title: Castling
rules.check: Check: the King is under attack. The side in check must get out of it by moving the King, blocking the attack or capturing the checking piece.
rules.clock: Each side has its own time budget. A 3+2 time control means 3 minutes to start, plus 2 seconds added after each move. Running out of time loses the game.
rules.draw.2: Insufficient material to checkmate, for example only two Kings, or a King with one Knight or one Bishop.
rules.draw.3: The same position occurs three times.
rules.draw.4: 50-move rule: 50 consecutive moves by each side with no pawn move and no capture.
rules.draw.5: Both players agree to a draw.
rules.draw.6: One side runs out of time but the other side lacks the material to checkmate.
rules.draw.title: Draws
rules.end.title: Check, checkmate and stalemate
rules.ep.text: When an enemy Pawn moves 2 squares from its starting position and lands right next to your Pawn, you may capture it as if it had moved only 1 square. This is allowed only on the very next move.
rules.ep.title: En passant
rules.goal.p1: Chess is played on an 8 × 8 board. Each side has 16 pieces: 1 King, 1 Queen, 2 Rooks, 2 Bishops, 2 Knights and 8 Pawns. White always moves first, then the players take turns, one move each.
rules.goal.p2: The goal is to checkmate the opponent's King: attack it so that there is no way to escape.
rules.goal.p3: When setting up, the right-hand corner square nearest each player is a light square, and each Queen starts on the square of her own colour.
rules.goal.title: The board and the goal
rules.legend: Dots: squares the piece can move to. Red rings: squares where the Pawn can capture.
rules.mate: Checkmate: the King is in check and there is no way to escape. The side delivering checkmate wins.
rules.move.B: Moves any number of squares diagonally, so it always stays on squares of one colour.
rules.move.K: Moves 1 square in any direction. It may not move onto a square attacked by an enemy piece.
rules.move.N: Moves in an L shape: 2 squares in one direction, then 1 square to the side. It is the only piece that can jump over others.
rules.move.P: Moves straight forward 1 square (2 squares on its first move) but captures 1 square diagonally forward. Pawns never move backwards.
rules.move.Q: Moves any number of squares along ranks, files and diagonals. It is the most powerful piece.
rules.move.R: Moves any number of squares along ranks and files.
rules.notation.p1: Each square is named by its file (a–h) and rank (1–8), for example e4. Pieces are written with English letters: K = King, Q = Queen, R = Rook, B = Bishop, N = Knight; Pawns have no letter.
rules.notation.p2: Examples: Nf3 (Knight to f3), exd5 (e-pawn captures on d5), O-O (kingside castling), O-O-O (queenside castling), e8=Q (promotion to Queen). + means check, # means checkmate.
rules.notation.title: Clocks and move notation
rules.pieces.title: How each piece moves
rules.promo.text: A Pawn that reaches the last rank must be exchanged for a Queen, Rook, Bishop or Knight of the same colour. Players usually choose a Queen.
rules.promo.title: Promotion
rules.resignTime: You also win if your opponent resigns or runs out of time.
rules.special.title: Special moves
rules.stalemate: Stalemate: the side to move has no legal move but its King is not in check. The game is a draw.
rules.tips.1: Control the centre (d4, e4, d5, e5) with Pawns and minor pieces.
rules.tips.2: Develop Knights and Bishops early, and avoid moving the same piece many times in the opening.
rules.tips.3: Castle early to keep your King safe.
rules.tips.4: Before every move, check what your opponent just threatened: a check, a capture or another tactic.
rules.tips.5: Don't bring your Queen out too early, it can easily be chased around and you lose time.
rules.tips.6: Solve puzzles every day to spot mating patterns faster.
rules.tips.title: Tips for beginners
rules.value: Reference values: Pawn 1, Knight 3, Bishop 3, Rook 5, Queen 9. The King is priceless, because losing it loses the game.
